coverage.sampleScope: samples counts both complete raw recordings; pairedSamples counts only retained paired five-second intervals in the six-day analysis.

summary.interpretation: Sleep-like rest from collar stillness. Shared timing does not establish sleeping in the same place or interaction.

runWindow.description: Full local calendar day; human sleep hours are 22:00–06:00.

method.movementUnit: mg = thousandths of gravitational acceleration; movement is the root-sum of within-epoch acceleration variances across three axes.
method.movementMeaning: Higher values mean more variable collar movement. These are not steps, calories, distance, or a validated exercise measure. Grooming and head movements contribute.
method.restMeaning: Sleep-like rest is sustained low movement with stable posture. Quiet wakefulness can qualify; this does not measure physiological sleep.
method.restRuleText: Five-second intervals below 20 mg with less than 5 degrees of posture change, in bouts of at least five minutes that are at least 90% quiet. Internal breaks of at most 30 seconds may join a bout; the breaks themselves do not count as rest.
method.pairing: Both cats use exactly the same valid five-second intervals. Each interval needs at least 4.9 seconds of sample coverage. Missing time earns no movement or rest credit.
method.normalization: Rest hours per period are the observed rest proportion times 24, 16, or 8 hours. Daytime overlap is proportion times 16 hours; full-day overlap is proportion times 24 hours. This scales for 80 excluded daytime seconds rather than treating them as stillness.
method.schemaUnits: summary preserves the analysis field names and units. hourly, days.hourly, and days.timeline use mg for peach/toast and 0–1 proportions for rest and coverage. daily peachRest/toastRest and bothRestHours24h use hours per 24h; daily bothRestHours uses hours per 16h daytime. daily bothRest remains a 0–1 full-day proportion. overlap.runs cover 0–1440 clock minutes with five-second precision; state 4 explicitly preserves missing paired data. overlap.summary and overlap.hourly remain daytime statistics.
method.restAlignment: The different-date baseline matches each Peach date to every other Toast date at the same clock times. It is a descriptive comparison, not a randomized experiment or evidence of causation.
limitations: Six shared days describe this recording, not stable lifelong traits.
Device wall clocks are assumed to be aligned Pacific local time; that alignment was not independently verified.
Changing the stillness threshold can reverse which cat appears to rest longer.
Simultaneous rest does not establish co-location, interaction, or one cat influencing the other.
The unusually quiet September 4 was identified after examining the data; it does not establish a cause or health problem.

population.conclusion: These recordings cannot reliably rank Peach or Toast against most cats.
population.reason: A fair population comparison needs the same sensor, processing, activity definition, and cats of comparable ages and lifestyles. Collar movement, including grooming, is not interchangeable with walking or exercise time.
population.rhythm: Morning and evening activity peaks and substantial quiet time resemble patterns reported in other housed cats; familiar timing does not establish an average total activity level.
population.interpretation: Use this week as a personal baseline for each cat, not a population percentile or a medical assessment.
